memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. They also overlaid the crossbars with gold." - Exod 36:29-30, 34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a detail worth pausing on. The frames were acacia wood — ordinary desert timber, hard and plain. And they were completely overlaid with gold.

The wood did not become gold. It was still wood underneath, still cut from a scrubby desert tree. But it was covered so thoroughly that what anyone saw was gold.

That is a picture of what God has done for us. We are not made worthy in ourselves. Our nature is not transformed into something divine. But we are covered — clothed with Christ (Gal 3:27), credited with a righteousness that was never ours to begin with (2 Cor 5:21).

Some people find this troubling, as though it makes faith a cover-up. It does not. God knows exactly what the wood is. He chose the wood. He also chose to cover it in gold and place it in His dwelling.

And the covering was not partial. Every frame, every crossbar, even the rings. Nothing was left exposed.

Do not spend your life trying to become acacia that looks like gold on its own. You cannot. Receive the covering.

Then live as what you now are — plain material that God has claimed, covered and set in the place where He dwells.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to make yourself acceptable to God, or receive His covering?
2. What "wood" in you are you ashamed of that God already knows about?
3. How does being clothed with Christ change how you see yourself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am plain wood, and You have covered me in Christ. Thank You for choosing me and clothing me. Amen.
